full.quality_rule: FULL keeps the existing high bar: explain a concrete technical/workflow change, production or pipeline consequence, and an actionable adoption test, risk, limitation, or maturity judgment. Broad admission does not lower the FULL evidence bar.

brief.quality_rule: BRIEF is the normal destination for an admission-pass item whose evidence cannot honestly support FULL depth. A verified single-source item may publish as BRIEF when claims are scoped to what the source actually demonstrates. Tutorials, tips, small tools, shader demos, community experiences, animation references and visual-development showcases do not need FULL-level evidence to be admitted when they provide at least one concrete production/reference takeaway. State the known fact/value and explicitly mark uncertainty or maturity limits.

top5_policy.rule: Homepage TOP5 selects the highest-ranked FULL items first. If fewer than the configured TOP5 count are available, fill only the remaining slots with the highest-ranked BRIEF survivors. BRIEF remains BRIEF, must stay visibly identified as limited-depth analysis, and must never be upgraded, padded, or used to displace an available FULL item.

quality_rule: Admission and evidence-depth classification are separate. First apply config/intelligence-v2.json#collection.admission_policy: if the item is verifiable, relevant or transferable, unpublished or substantively changed, and has at least one concrete production/technical/workflow/testing/animation-reference/visual-development takeaway, it is worth inclusion. Then classify by evidence depth: FULL for 3-5 source-supported substantive blocks; otherwise BRIEF for 1-2 honest limited-depth blocks. Limited evidence depth alone must not cause REJECT. Ranking handles narrower impact. REJECT is reserved for hard admission failures only. Never fabricate or pad evidence to upgrade BRIEF to FULL.
legacy_policy: Dates before tiered_effective_date keep the prior FULL-only depth behavior and are not retroactively reclassified.
